security_audit.summary: Reviewed all 400 presented findings; most are documentation, secret-hygiene checks, or scoped local tooling. Confirmed shell injection and identified unsafe rollback guidance, empty final-review ranges, untrusted prompt content, and plaintext remote authentication. No evidence found of intentional exfiltration; 1,468 omitted static matches still require manual review before publication. Static review was capped at 400/1868 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 1468 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Custom browser launching permits shell substitution in the URL.
remediation.suggestion: Replace cp.exec with execFile and explicit arguments. Validate URL hostnames and avoid treating JSON string escaping as shell escaping.

remediation.issue: Registry directory checks execute editable Markdown cells through a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace awk system() with directory checks that treat paths as data. Restrict registry paths to validated descendants of the execution store.

remediation.issue: The final-review default can compare HEAD against itself.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve the recorded plan fork revision and review its cumulative changes through HEAD. Reject equal revisions when implementation commits are expected.

remediation.issue: Recovery instructions can revert mixed user and agent edits.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before destructive recovery. Preserve a patch and revert only verified agent-owned changes.

remediation.issue: Direct remote companion access transmits bearer authentication over plaintext.
remediation.suggestion: Keep loopback binding by default. Require an encrypted tunnel or TLS reverse proxy for remote use and support secure WebSocket URLs.

remediation.issue: Editable review prose can become worker instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Mark inserted findings as untrusted evidence. Explicitly preserve higher-priority instructions and reject requests to bypass security checks or approvals.

remediation.issue: The static catalog excludes 1,468 repeated or lower-priority matches.
remediation.suggestion: Complete manual review of the omitted matches before publication. Do not interpret this completed adjudication as clearance of unpresented findings.

semantic_findings.title: Final Review Can Inspect an Empty Commit Range
semantic_findings.description: Without an explicit base, final review defaults both revisions to the current HEAD. The required whole-branch review can therefore omit every implementation change.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script never initializes plan_branch, so the normal fallback selects HEAD for both revisions. It then dispatches a final reviewer with that range.

semantic_findings.title: Recovery Guidance Can Discard Uncommitted User Work
semantic_findings.description: Drift Recovery recommends "git checkout -- <paths>" for uncommitted edits without requiring approval or isolating agent-owned changes. Mixed user edits can be lost.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The recovery instruction explicitly recommends reverting paths without an ownership check. A broader destructive-action stop exists, but this recovery step omits it.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Companion Authentication Uses Plaintext Transport
semantic_findings.description: Non-loopback binding is supported, but companion HTTP and WebSocket URLs use plaintext transport. Direct remote access exposes session keys and screen data to interception.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The displayed session URL uses http and the browser connection uses ws. Loopback is the default, but direct remote binding has no transport encryption.

semantic_findings.title: Review Findings Enter Worker Instructions Without a Trust Boundary
semantic_findings.description: Review findings are inserted verbatim into worker prompts. A manipulated verdict can supply behavioral instructions instead of evidence unless the worker preserves instruction hierarchy.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The dispatcher copies editable verdict prose into FINDINGS, and the renderer inserts replacement text unchanged. No evidence found of an embedded attack payload.

high_findings.title: Environment file access
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The custom launcher passes a URL to a shell using JSON.stringify, which leaves shell substitutions active. A crafted URL hostname can execute commands.

high_findings.title: Ruby/PHP system() call
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: An editable registry cell is concatenated into awk system() without shell quoting. Shell metacharacters in that cell can execute arbitrary local commands.

high_findings.title: Final Review Can Inspect an Empty Commit Range
high_findings.description: Without an explicit base, final review defaults both revisions to the current HEAD. The required whole-branch review can therefore omit every implementation change.
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script never initializes plan_branch, so the normal fallback selects HEAD for both revisions. It then dispatches a final reviewer with that range.

high_findings.title: Review Findings Enter Worker Instructions Without a Trust Boundary
high_findings.description: Review findings are inserted verbatim into worker prompts. A manipulated verdict can supply behavioral instructions instead of evidence unless the worker preserves instruction hierarchy.
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The dispatcher copies editable verdict prose into FINDINGS, and the renderer inserts replacement text unchanged. No evidence found of an embedded attack payload.

medium_findings.title: Recovery Guidance Can Discard Uncommitted User Work
medium_findings.description: Drift Recovery recommends "git checkout -- <paths>" for uncommitted edits without requiring approval or isolating agent-owned changes. Mixed user edits can be lost.
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The recovery instruction explicitly recommends reverting paths without an ownership check. A broader destructive-action stop exists, but this recovery step omits it.

medium_findings.title: Remote Companion Authentication Uses Plaintext Transport
medium_findings.description: Non-loopback binding is supported, but companion HTTP and WebSocket URLs use plaintext transport. Direct remote access exposes session keys and screen data to interception.
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The displayed session URL uses http and the browser connection uses ws. Loopback is the default, but direct remote binding has no transport encryption.

low_findings.title: Environment variable access (dot notation)
low_findings.confidence_reasoning: The custom launcher passes a URL to a shell using JSON.stringify, which leaves shell substitutions active. A crafted URL hostname can execute commands.

content.value_statement: Long coding projects lose context, decisions, and review evidence across sessions. Executor records initiative state and coordinates phase routing, task dispatch, and approval gates.
actual_capabilities: Route substantial requests to initiative phases and identify work that does not need an initiative.
Maintain initiative identifiers, tracked documentation, and separate execution records.
Render registered worker prompts and record task dispatches, reports, verdicts, and rulings.
Manage task branches and optional Git worktrees with review-dependent merge checks.
Track worker heartbeats and support bounded revival or fresh dispatch.
Scan Executor artifacts for credential-shaped content without printing matched values.
limitations: Full phase workflows depend on companion Executor skills and prompt templates outside this package.
Scripts require a Git repository, Bash, and common command-line tools; the optional visual companion also requires Node.js.
Secret detection uses known patterns and does not guarantee that artifacts contain no sensitive data.
Security concerns and omitted static matches require further review before publication or unattended use.

use_cases.title: Resume a Multi-Component Feature
use_cases.description: Recover the recorded initiative phase, outstanding tasks, and required approvals before continuing a feature across sessions.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Reviewed Migration Work
use_cases.description: Organize migration requirements, task branches, review rounds, and decision records within one initiative.

use_cases.title: Inspect Initiative Readiness
use_cases.description: Check recorded phase gates, artifact references, task outcomes, and verification evidence before preparing a handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Right Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess whether [request] needs an Executor initiative. Identify its lasting deliverable and suggest the appropriate starting phase without changing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: decide whether a request needs initiative tracking.

prompt_templates.title: Resume an Initiative
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the repository and recorded indexes for [initiative ID]. Report the current phase, last recorded event, and next required approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: recover context after a session interruption.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Reviewed Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the artifacts for [initiative ID] before planning. Identify missing specifications, unresolved decisions, and required plan-regression checks before any task dispatch.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: establish readiness for reviewed implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate an Approved Execution
prompt_templates.prompt: Coordinate [approved plan path] using registered workers and recorded rulings. Preserve user edits and stop for destructive operations, security-sensitive actions, or missing approvals.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate task execution after reviewing the security concerns and confirming prerequisites.

output_examples.input: Resume the initiative after its planning session.
output: Last recorded event: the plan was drafted; execution mode remains undecided.
Next action: present the recorded options for human approval before dispatching implementation.

output_examples.input: Check whether the plan is ready for handoff.
output: A completed task has no clean review verdict.
Record the missing review and verify the cumulative final-review range before requesting handoff approval.

output_examples.input: Scan initiative artifacts without exposing credentials.
output: Credential-shaped content was detected in an artifact.
The scan reports the file, line, and credential category without printing its value.
Handoff remains blocked until the human resolves the finding and rotates committed credentials where necessary.

best_practices: Read current repository state and recorded indexes before resuming an initiative.
Use registered scripts for identifiers and transitions, and obtain explicit approval at phase boundaries.
Use synthetic mockup data, review the security concerns, and scan both artifact stores before handoff.
anti_patterns: Creating initiative records for questions, typos, or other work without a lasting deliverable.
Treating generated artifacts, recorded approvals, or a secret scan as proof that unattended execution is safe.
Discarding uncommitted edits, exposing the companion directly over plaintext networks, or accepting untrusted prompt instructions.

faq.question: What is an Executor initiative?
faq.answer: An initiative groups a lasting coding deliverable with its identifiers, phase records, design documents, plans, and execution evidence.

faq.question: Should I use it for a small fix?
faq.answer: Not for a typo, one-line fix, or question. Use it when the work needs durable planning and review records.

faq.question: Does this package include every phase skill?
faq.answer: No. The router and dispatch registry reference additional Executor phase skills and worker templates that must be available separately.

faq.question: How does session recovery work?
faq.answer: Repository state, initiative indexes, execution records, and worker heartbeat files identify the recorded phase and appropriate next action.

faq.question: Can I commit the execution records?
faq.answer: The execution store is ignored by default. Commit it only after explicit user approval and a review for secrets and personal data.

faq.question: Is unattended execution cleared by this audit?
faq.answer: No. Command-injection risks, review integrity concerns, and omitted static matches require remediation or manual review before relying on unattended execution.
